short: Denoising-autoencoder audio is new to AVSR but rests on one corpus; the CNN is the authors' uncited 2014 design; weights, depth and read-out are tuned on the test words (M12 behind).
position: The paper changes decoding (M06): a denoising autoencoder cleans 11-frame MFCC windows, a per-speaker CNN turns mouth crops into phoneme posteriors, and a multi-stream HMM fuses both with hand-set weights [@noda2015audiovisual]. The audio denoiser is new to AVSR (0 of 65 prior AVSR studies name a learned denoiser, pattern match, Appendix), but it is shown on one corpus of six male speakers with no per-speaker breakdown or repeated runs, so M06 is standard. The CNN is the authors' own uncited Interspeech 2014 design, three months older [@noda2014lipreading], and multi-stream HMM fusion was the usual design (29 of 65, Appendix). Evaluation (M12) is behind: stream weights and autoencoder depth are chosen on the test words, whereas read priors tuned weights on held-out data and tested unseen speakers [@papandreou2009adaptive], [@potamianos2003audiovisual]. The "additional 10 %" gain at 0 dB (Sec. 6.5) is a best-of-11 upper bound from one run.
